item.title: 14 dead, dozens injured in northern China high-rise building fire
item.description: Fourteen people died and dozens more were hospitalised after a fire broke out in a high-rise building in northern China on Sunday. The fire erupted at around 5pm in the Haosheng International Apartment building in Taiyuan, the capital city of Shanxi province, according to the Yingze district government. It was put out by around 7pm and rescue efforts ended at around 8.30pm, the authorities said. That night, 38 people were sent to hospital, among whom five died. By Monday morning, the death toll...

item.title: Malaysia’s Melaka could get new capital in Kota Laksamana if Barisan wins poll
item.description: Kota Laksamana in Melaka could be developed into Malaysian state’s new capital if Umno-led Barisan Nasional wins the seat in Saturday’s poll, according to caretaker chief minister Ab Rauf Yusoh. He said the proposed transformation would be supported by the Straits of Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone, which would bring together tourism, commercial and industrial activities along the state’s waterfront. “Kota Laksamana will become the state capital of Melaka. That is what I hope for,” he said...

item.title: Citybus driver arrested after fatally knocking down pedestrian in North Point
item.description: Hong Kong police have arrested a Citybus driver after his vehicle struck and killed an elderly man in North Point. The fatal incident happened at the junction of King’s Road and Tin Chong Street at around 8am, with police and ambulance personnel arriving at the scene after a report made by the bus driver. item.title: Child abuse cases rise in Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore. Why?
item.description: Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore have all recorded rising numbers of child abuse cases in recent years, but child welfare advocates say this may be a sign of progress rather than worsening violence, as greater awareness and improved reporting bring more cases to the attention of authorities. “The good news is that more people are reporting,” said Hartini Zainuddin, a veteran advocate for abused children in Malaysia.
